claims.text: The initial Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy is a single-phase BCC solid solution.
Compositional differences between dendritic and interdendritic regions cause asymmetric XRD peaks in the initial alloy.
The initial alloy has significantly lower room-temperature fracture strain than theoretically expected or reported for similar alloys.
Adding approximately 4 at.% Cr to Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr drives formation of a complex multicomponent Laves phase.
The Cr-induced Laves phase is enriched in Cr and Ta.
The Cr-induced Laves phase has a volume fraction of approximately 4%.
A negative Cr-Ta mixing enthalpy favors Cr-Ta intermetallic or Laves-phase formation.
The secondary Laves phase forms a reticulated or interconnected network along dendritic regions or boundaries.
The interconnected Laves-phase network forces crack deflection and branching and thereby impedes crack extension.
Crack deflection by the Laves-phase network increases fracture toughness and room-temperature fracture strain.
Cr dissolved in the BCC matrix increases lattice distortion.
Cr-induced lattice distortion causes solid-solution hardening by reducing dislocation mobility.
Cr has a smaller atomic radius than the average atomic radius of the base Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy.
Adding Cr causes a measurable contraction of the BCC lattice parameter.

High-resolution XRD combined with EDS mapping can distinguish micro-segregation effects from Cr-specific phase formation by correlating local chemistry and phase identity with diffraction-peak shifts.
The Laves phase can be identified as a distinct phase with a specific crystal structure and composition using XRD, EDS, and TEM.
Processing conditions such as cooling rate and heat treatment may change the volume fraction and morphology of the secondary phase.
Minor elements or impurities may alter interactions between the Laves phase and the BCC matrix.
Failure to detect the Laves phase, obtain an approximately 4% phase fraction, observe BCC lattice contraction, or improve fracture strain would falsify the corresponding parts of the hypothesis.
